audit_notes: Slip: 30 nm is at the upper end of measured water slip on hydrophobic smooth surfaces (10-30 nm); adjusted to 2e-8 m for consistency with the brush literature. b+ = 0.004 -> expected gain 0.02%: no drag change versus a clean FR hull. Roughness 0.5 um = 0.09 viscous units: hydraulically smooth (both design and baseline). The real value of a hard, smooth topcoat is that roughness stays low over years (damaged FR coatings reach 50-150 um roughness, k+ = 10-30, i.e. +3-8% friction), but that is a comparison against an aged baseline and cannot be computed here. Structural: glass-ceramic/ sol-gel silica-siloxane has E ~5-20 GPa and failure strain ~0.2-0.5%, while hull plating sees strains up to ~0.1-0.15% (hogging/sagging, thermal) and local impacts; cracking and spalling are likely on steel unless the layer is thin (<20 um) on a tough primer. The 5 nm PDMS brush wears off at first mechanical cleaning. Baseline: smooth FR, slip 0.

performance_gain.label: Skin-friction reduction vs clean FR hull
